one_line: Call out the parent's moment in the first words, name the product by second 2, and show it in use.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 a woman at a marina stands behind a stroller with a baby, a hand near her mouth. Text: 'אם אתם טסים לחו"ל'. At 0:02 she carries the folded stroller, 'anex Air Z Plus' appears; at 0:03 she opens it.
q1_hook.why: A parent with a trip coming is named in the first words (H1, K7). The stroller is on screen at 0:00, handled and named by 0:03 (S1, H2). A person on camera, voice and word-by-word text start together (H4, H6).

beats.what: Marina, 'אם אתם טסים לחו"ל'; she carries the folded stroller, opens it one-handed; 'anex Air Z Plus'
beats.why: Callout, product name and the fold in 3 s.

beats.what: She pushes it by a hotel pool, a partner and toddler at the water; 'חיפשנו פתרון'
Close-ups: reclined seat, hood vent, wheels, basket; 'לשנ"צים', 'פתחי אוורור', 'גלגלים שסופגים זעזועים', 'וסל גדול'
beats.why: One feature a second, each shown as named.

beats.what: She folds the stroller and lifts it by the handle; 'שתמיד יוצאים איתנו'
Airport: she folds the stroller at a gate; cross-dissolve to a plane; 'אחרי שבוע שלם בחו"ל'
Pool, a baby with a soft book beside the folded stroller, the beach; 'אם אתם נוסעים לחו"ל בקרוב'
beats.why: The holiday made simple; the callout repeats.

beats.what: She stands in a sunny street, hand to chin; 'אל תשכחו את הטיולון הזה'

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: None. The closing 'אל תשכחו את הטיולון הזה' is a reminder, not an ask. The caption asks nothing.
q2_flow.why: The product is in every shot and a new picture arrives about every 1.3 s, each tied to the word said (R3). The callout returns at 0:25, so a late viewer gets it too (H1). The holiday promise is paid off by airport and hotel scenes (K2). It ends right after the closing line (R1).

q3_cta.what: No ask in the video. The last line, said and shown: 'אל תשכחו את הטיולון הזה' (0:27 to 0:28). Caption: 'להשיג בלעדית ברשת בייביסטאר', then the tags. No link, code or price.
q3_cta.why: A reminder, not an action, and where to buy sits only in the caption (C6). A viewer who wants it has no code, link or price (C3). One message throughout, but a soft one (C1).

q4_shown.what: The brown stroller with a baby at the marina from 0:00; folded and opened one-handed 0:02; close-ups of seat, vent, wheels, basket 0:08 to 0:14; carried folded 0:15; an airport, a plane 0:17 to 0:21; pool, room, beach 0:22 to 0:26. No price.
q4_shown.why: The stroller is handled in the first 3 s, and each feature is shown at once as a close-up (S1, F4). Use in many travel places with a baby and a partner makes the holiday believable (K5). The 'fits the cabin' claim is only implied, with no label or size shown (K4).

q5_edit.what: About 22 shots in 29 s (1.3 s each): hard cuts on the words, one cross-dissolve at 0:18 to 0:20; no speed changes seen. Small white text in 1 to 3 word chunks mid-frame. Ends on a medium shot of her with the stroller.
q5_edit.why: A cut about every second, each on a new feature, keeps information flowing (R3), but is faster than the 2 to 5 s the research suggests (E2), and the small text changes too fast to read (T5). It ends as it began, on her, with no tail (R4, E8).

q6_topic.what: A compact travel stroller for flying and holidays: fold, airport, hotel. Serves parents with a trip coming.
q6_topic.why: A clear buying moment, an upcoming trip, is named in the first words and repeated at 0:25 (K7). The features answer a real travel worry (K6). The mood is calm and aspirational, not a high-arousal peak (K1).

q7_filmed.what: Phone, mostly static at eye level and low angle: close-ups of seat, vent, wheels and basket; wide airport and hotel clips with other people; she appears at the marina and in a street. Bright daylight. Some clips look shot by a second person.
q7_filmed.why: Bright travel light and static shots keep the product clear (F7, F4). Many locations and people make it hard for a solo creator to copy, and it reads polished more than homemade (H8).

q8_text.on_screen: Small white sans-serif words, 1 to 3 per cut, at about 48 to 55% of the frame height, the key word bold: 'אם אתם טסים לחו"ל' (0:00, larger), 'anex Air Z Plus' (0:02, large Latin), 'חיפשנו פתרון' (0:05), 'לשנ"צים' (0:10), 'גלגלים שסופגים זעזועים' (0:13), 'אחרי שבוע שלם בחו"ל' (0:18), 'אל תשכחו את הטיולון הזה' (0:27). No CTA box.
q8_text.caption: 'אם יש פריט אחד שלא הייתי מוותרת עליו בחופשה עם הבייבי'. Short, about 45 words: 'זה טיולון מורשה טיסה של Anex', a result line, 'להשיג בלעדית ברשת בייביסטאר', two brand tags, five generic hashtags. 'בשיתוף' near the end. No question.
q8_text.why: Short text works muted (T1) and the product name is large text by 0:02 (T3), but words change every second, over the product shots (T5, T2). The caption names the product and the occasion early, with generic hashtags (T7). 'בשיתוף' sits near the end (T8, S7).

weak_points: Small text that changes every second; footage that needs a trip, a partner and a baby; the cabin-size claim never shown; no code, link or price; the partnership word near the end.
lumebook_takeaway: Open with 'if you are about to...' for a gift moment, name the book by second 2, then one feature per shot with one-line captions. Hands only.
not_verified: Whether the airport and hotel clips are her own (other people appear, in different clothes). Whether the man in the plane is stowing the folded stroller or a bag. The price. Music (none evident). The paid label (0 per media info). Correction: the product name appears at 0:02 to 0:03, over the shot where she carries and opens the stroller.
